output.summary: Perennial bulb-forming flowering plant native to Central Asia, northeastern Iran and the Himalayan foothills. Its strong-smelling bulb typically contains 10–20 cloves, while sulfur compounds create its pungent flavour. The cloves are eaten raw or cooked, and cooking considerably mellows and sweetens them.
output.edibilityNote: Cloves are eaten raw or cooked; immature leaves, flowers and scapes are also edible.
